33.0.s.en: (1) The first stage: from Rameses to the wilderness of Sinai

33.0.0.en: With their armies: that is, they went out with all their men numbered for war.

33.0.1.en: This is the opening of the whole chapter: "These are the journeys of the children of Israel". It adds that this historical record is from the day of their departure from the land of Egypt with all their men numbered for war, everyone aged 20 years and above. The expression "under the hand of Moses and Aaron" means under the supervision and direction of the civil leader "Moses" and the spiritual leader "Aaron" the priest.

33.1.0.en: Their goings out: that is, the places from which the people began to move or set out.

33.1.1.en: It was God, by His providence, who commanded Moses to write this historical record for his people, so that he might review with them all the places they had passed through, their pleasant and painful events, and His work with them. So we are before a spiritual, historical and geographical record that summarizes and reviews for the people God's being with them on a journey that took 40 years. Verses (1, 2) are considered the introduction of this chapter, which is a comprehensive historical record of all the movements of the children of Israel until their arrival at the east of the Jordan.

33.2.0.en: The first station of departure was "Rameses", now known as the area of "San el-Hagar"

33.2.1.en: in Sharqia (Ex 12:37), where the people ate the Passover on the evening of the fourteenth day of the month of Nisan, which God made the first of the months of the religious year (ch. 28:16). On the second day after eating the Passover, the fifteenth of the month, all the people moved, leaving the place. The expression "with an high hand" points to God's mighty work with the people in the ten plagues, especially the last plague of the firstborn. This departure was before the eyes of all the Egyptians, who did not prevent the people of the children of Israel from leaving and quitting the city (Maps 7, 8).

33.3.0.en: This verse shows the Egyptians' preoccupation and their great grief for their firstborn who had died, and that they were busy burying them. The people were pained in all this, looking to their God, who "executed judgments" upon their gods, that is, that the Lord by His work and His high arm declared that He is the only true God, while the rest of the gods are vain and the work of human hands and cannot do anything before Him. They did not protect the Egyptian people from the plagues, and were not able to prevent the people of the children of Israel from leaving the land of Egypt.

33.3.1.en: The Exodus and the first stages in the wilderness, Map (7) Map (8)

33.4.0.en: If "Rameses" was the first point of departure, "Succoth" was likewise the first resting station after the people moved. Succoth means "booths", and it lies between present-day Ismailia and Suez, but a little toward the west.

33.5.0.en: The next rest was at "Etham", which is south of the Bitter Lakes and northwest of the Gulf of Suez. From there they saw the desert of Sinai before them, but they had not yet crossed (meaning that if the Suez Canal had existed in that time, they were still west of it.)

33.6.0.en: The people went down south instead of going north as far as "Pi-hahiroth", which lies west of the Gulf of Suez at its northern end, so the waters of the sea were before them, and at this point Migdol and Pi-hahiroth were to their north, while Baal-zephon lay to their south. From this point the people crossed the Red Sea after Moses stretched out his rod and touched its waters with it (Ex 14:15-30), and they went three days in "the wilderness of Etham", which is the one mentioned in (v. 6). We know from this that Etham was a wilderness extending west and east ("which the canal now divides"), south of Ismailia and north of Suez, and "Marah" was the first station of encampment after the crossing, where the people found bitter water and murmured, and when Moses cast a tree into it, it became sweet (Ex 15:23-25). It is noted that God led them away from the usual road for reaching Palestine from Egypt, which runs alongside the Mediterranean, that is, the direction of El-Arish and Rafah, because of the many Egyptian garrisons there that would have stopped their march, and He guided them with the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire southward to the Gulf of Suez, where nothing would hinder them, and He parted the Red Sea before them, that is, the Gulf of Suez, and they crossed into the wilderness of Sinai.

33.7.0.en: Then the direction was downward alongside the Gulf of Suez, so they left "Marah" for "Elim", and there they found water for rest (Ex 15:27), twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees, and after staying a while in Elim they camped for a period alongside the Red Sea. Note the correspondence between this number and the number of the Fathers the Apostles, the pure twelve disciples, as well as the seventy apostles whom the Lord Christ sent to the regions of the world, who became water of refreshment and spiritual satisfaction for the whole world.(

33.8.0.en: The wilderness of Sin: it lies southwest of the wilderness of Sinai alongside the Gulf of Suez in the direction of the present city of El-Tor, and it is the place where the people murmured against God for food (Ex 16) (Map 2), and the Lord gave them manna in it. From the wilderness of Sin, in the direction north toward Rephidim, they stopped at two successive places, "Dophkah and Alush", and these two sites are not mentioned in the book of Exodus because of their smallness.

33.9.0.en: Rephidim was one of the famous stations in the people's journey, because in it the people murmured for water, and because of this murmuring this place was also given the name "Massah and Meribah", that is, "temptation and murmuring". In this place Moses met his father-in-law Jethro (Ex 18), and in it also the people were victorious in their war against Amalek.

33.10.0.en: The people reached the wilderness of Sinai, which lies northeast of the wilderness of Sin, and stayed in it for nearly a year, for all the preceding journeys took between two and three months. The wilderness of Sinai witnessed many events, the most important of which were:

33.10.1.en: 1- The seeing of the glory of the Lord and the receiving of the Ten Commandments (Ex 19, 20).

33.10.2.en: 2- The building of the tabernacle of meeting (Ex 40:1, 2 - 16:17).

33.10.3.en: 3- The receiving of the laws of the Levites (Ex 21-24).

33.10.4.en: 4- The first numbering of the people by Moses, Aaron and the heads of the people (ch. 1).

33.10.5.en: God led His people in the wilderness of Sinai with the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire, but the people murmured at every problem instead of turning to God in prayer. Be confident that your God loves you and arranges good for you, and you will enjoy this care if you rely on Him. If you find any difficulties, ask for His help to support you, so that you fulfill His will and rejoice in His ordering of your life.

33.11.s.en: (2) The second stage: arrival at Kadesh-barnea

33.11.0.en: The inspired text mentions here arrival at "Kibroth-hattaavah" immediately after the wilderness of Sinai, but we know from (ch. 11:3) that a short rest preceded "Kibroth-hattaavah", in the place called "Taberah", which means "burning", because the fire was kindled in their tents as a result of their murmuring. As for "Kibroth-hattaavah", it was spoken of before in (ch. 11:34), and we remind the dear reader here that its meaning is the graves of lust, where the people ate the quails greedily! ... And God punished them for their lust, and many of the people died.

33.12.0.en: Hazeroth: a name meaning enclosures or settlements.

33.12.1.en: It is the station following Kibroth-hattaavah, and it is the place where Miriam, the sister of Moses, was punished by being put out of the camp for seven days, stricken with leprosy, when she spoke evil of Moses (ch. 11:35, ch. 12).

33.13.0.en: Rithmah: a place considered to belong to Kadesh-barnea, and it was so named for a kind of tree in it called "broom trees".

33.13.1.en: The people were stationed for a considerable time at Kadesh-barnea, and it witnessed events, the most important of which were:

33.13.2.en: 1- The sending of the spies and the story that followed it, of God's anger against the people for their fear and murmuring (chs. 13, 14).

33.13.3.en: 2- The murmuring of Korah, Dathan and Abiram because of the priesthood of Aaron and what happened afterward (ch. 16).

33.13.4.en: 3- From Kadesh began the journey of the people's wandering, according to the Lord's command, for about 38 years.

33.13.5.en: The people moved about in many places in the wilderness of Sinai, and this signifies the need for spiritual striving in our life on earth. Would that you, my brother, persevere in your striving throughout the stages of your life, and know that God looks with care on every toil you offer for His sake, and He is able to support you and reward you for all your labors.

33.14.s.en: (3) The journey of wandering and the return to Kadesh-barnea

33.14.0.en: Rithmah, or Kadesh-barnea, was in the wilderness of Zin (v. 36), and when God commanded them to begin moving on the journey of wandering, they headed to the wilderness of "Paran" and toward the Red Sea again, and they passed through many of the places mentioned in the following verses.

33.14.1.en: Rimmon-parez: its meaning is the pomegranate of breaking forth.

33.14.3.en: Rissah: a place lying northwest of Libnah.

33.14.4.en: Kehelathah: its meaning is an assembly.

33.14.5.en: Mount Shapher: the mount of beauty.

33.14.8.en: Tahath: its meaning is the lower place or the bottom.

33.14.9.en: Tarah: its meaning is the ibex, one of the animals of the desert, resembling gazelles.

33.14.11.en: Hashmonah: its meaning is the fertile valley.

33.14.12.en: Moseroth: its meaning is bonds, and it is the place of the burial of Aaron, and consequently we conclude that it was near Mount Hor, on which he died.

33.14.13.en: Bene-jaakan: it lies north of the Gulf of Suez.

33.14.14.en: Hor-hagidgad: it lies northeast of the Gulf of Suez.

33.14.15.en: Jotbathah: it is said to be the original name of the present Taba, which is at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba. Some think that it is between the wilderness of Sinai and the wilderness of Paran, near the Gulf of Suez on the east.

33.14.16.en: Ebronah: a passage, meaning a way, and it is a low oasis between "Jotbathah" and "Ezion-gaber".

33.14.17.en: Ezion-gaber: it is the last station in the journey of wandering, and it is at the head of the Gulf of Aqaba on the western side, near the present port of Eilat. It is a city well known in the history of the people, since the First Book of Kings (ch. 9:26, 10:32) mentions that King Solomon built a fleet of ships there.

33.15.1.en: From the starting point of the wandering the people returned once again to the wilderness of Zin, which is north of the wilderness of Sinai on the side of the Gulf of Aqaba, and then they were stationed again in its most famous city, Kadesh-barnea. There Miriam, the sister of Moses and Aaron, died (ch. 20:1), and there also Moses erred when he struck the rock contrary to what God had commanded him (ch. 20). So they moved from Kadesh-barnea after their murmuring against God and their refusal to enter the Promised Land, and God made them wander in the desert, and they went in different lines in all directions, and finally they returned from north of the Gulf of Suez to north of the Gulf of Aqaba and then to Kadesh-barnea again.

33.15.2.en: When you meet troubles in your life and do not reach your material goals quickly, do not be disturbed, for God keeps you away from evil, and when you submit to Him and believe in Him, He brings you back again to achieve your goals, but with a pure heart that relies on Him alone and not on the world.

33.16.s.en: (4) From Kadesh to the east of the Jordan

33.16.0.en: Mount Hor: it lies between the north of the Gulf of Aqaba and the south of the Dead Sea.

33.16.1.en: The people moved, leaving Kadesh-barnea for the last time, and their first stop was at Mount "Hor".

33.17.0.en: These two verses are a brief review of what was explained in detail in (ch. 20:

33.17.1.en: 22-29) of God's calling of Aaron, His telling Moses of his death, and his son Eleazar's taking over the headship of the priesthood, but here the age of Aaron at his death is stated specifically, which was (123 years.)

33.18.0.en: And king Arad the Canaanite heard: also a brief reference to what the chapter (21:1-3) had spoken of before, that this king, when he learned of the people's departure, went out against them and fought them, but God finally gave the victory to His people, who made a vow to God for the sake of this victory.

33.18.1.en: After that the fiery serpents attacked the people of God because of their murmuring, and then God healed them by means of the bronze serpent (ch. 21:5-9).

33.19.0.en: Mount Hor lies west of the Gulf of Aqaba, and had the Edomites allowed the people to pass, that would have saved much, but that did not happen, so the people were forced to go around Edom, which was the land of the descendants of Esau. The first station after Mount "Hor" was "Zalmonah", whose meaning is "the shade", and it is considered an extension of Mount Hor or one of its peaks. After it "Punon" is mentioned as the next station, which lies northwest of "Ezion-gaber" (v. 35), and after it was "Oboth", which lies north of the port of Eilat, and its meaning "near the water" expressed its location.

33.20.0.en: Iye-abarim: it lies southeast of Moab and is sometimes called Iim because it lies next to it, and some consider it a part of it.

33.20.1.en: With the people's arrival at "Abarim" they were on the border of the Moabites, east of the river Jordan (ch. 21:13).

33.21.0.en: "Dibon" was one of the cities of the Amorites, over whom and over their king "Sihon" the people were victorious. Its meaning was ruin, and the tribe of Gad asked for it as land for its cattle, and after Moses' agreement the land came to bear their name, "Dibon-gad"; see (ch. 32:2-5).

33.22.0.en: Then the journey was northward alongside the Jordan, and they took all the lands of the Midianites in the direction of the kingdom of Bashan, over which they were also victorious. In this northward journey the stations of the people's encampment and departure are mentioned, such as "Almon-diblathaim" and "the mountains of Abarim" (ch. 21:16-35). There they were victorious over Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan.

33.23.0.en: Then came their complete settlement in "the plains of Moab", east of the Jordan and opposite the city of Jericho, which lies on the opposite west bank. (v. 49) came to draw the boundaries of the people's settlement on the east of the Jordan in the plains of Moab. Its southern boundary was "Beth-jesimoth", lying north of the Dead Sea where the river Jordan flows into it, while the northern boundary was "Abel-shittim", lying on the river Jordan itself opposite Jericho.

33.23.1.en: It is observed that when the people encamped here, all the events from (ch. 22 to ch. 32) took place, the most important of which were:

33.23.2.en: a- The story of Balak and Balaam (chs. 22-24).

33.23.3.en: b- The people's falling into fornication with the Moabite women and God's striking the people with the plague (ch. 25).

33.23.4.en: c- The second numbering of the people (ch. 26).

33.23.5.en: d- The laws of the division of the land, its portions and proportions (ch. 26).

33.23.6.en: e- Moses' appointing Joshua as successor and leader of the people after seeing the land from Mount Abarim (ch. 27).

33.23.7.en: f- The laws of offerings and vows (chs. 28-30).

33.23.8.en: g- The fighting of the Midianites and the victory over them, and the request of Reuben and Gad to obtain land for their cattle (chs. 31, 32).

33.23.9.en: God preserved His people in all their movements because He was their leader by the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire, and whoever tried to oppose them, they were victorious over. Let God be a leader to you in your life, and you will be at ease, and even if some oppose you and try to trouble you, be confident that your God is with you, preserving you and bringing you through the troubles, and giving you victory over your enemies the demons, so that He keeps you pure at all times.

33.24.s.en: (5) Warnings concerning the possession of the new land

33.24.0.en: As the people settled after 40 years of wandering, and the land of Canaan lay opposite them, God tells them that they will cross into the land and possess it, and He reviews with them some last matters in the form of warnings, so that the people might avoid the dangers into which they might fall, as we shall see.

33.25.0.en: The first divine command and warning came as follows:

33.25.1.en: 1- Driving out all the inhabitants of the land: God knows the weakness of human nature, and knows too that any person is liable to be influenced by those around him, and for this reason He completely forbade the people to mingle with the other peoples whose land they would take. They must drive them out, because keeping them would mean the people's falling into fornication and idol worship, as happened before (ch. 25).

33.25.2.en: 2- Destroy all their pictures: that is, all the memorials, drawings and works of the molten idols and images which these peoples worshiped. The people of God had to destroy them utterly, for the same purpose as before.

33.25.3.en: 3- Pluck down their high places: the high places are elevated places such as hills, on which the pagan peoples set up their altars. God's command was that they be destroyed completely.

33.25.4.en: What God commanded His people here is a general commandment for us all, and the sum of what God said is: keep away from evil and all its traces, and do not keep anything of it around you or within you, so that Satan may find no way to remind you of what went before in order to make you fall again. Let us understand this and all pray with the Church, asking for God's help and crying out to Him with the words of the Divine Liturgy: "Every thought that does not please Your goodness, O God, lover of mankind, let it be far from us."

33.26.0.en: God calls His people to possess the land after He has destroyed its wicked inhabitants, who had corrupted it for a long time. But He reminds His people that He is the owner of this gift, and God wants us by this to learn that He is the source and maker of all good things, so that we live a life of thanksgiving.

33.27.0.en: Here God repeats to His people His just commandments on the way of dividing the land, in which justice is observed between the number of members of the tribe and the area of land they possess, and that the division is to be by lot, so that the people might avoid entering into disputes over the portions (ch. 26:52-56).

33.28.0.en: Pricks: the prick is a metal projection in the heel of a horseman's boot with which he pricks his horse to urge it to run fast.

33.28.1.en: After God commanded the people what must be done with the peoples of the land (v. 52), He reviews with them a second time in another form that they must not be lax in carrying out all that He commanded, otherwise the consequence of this laxity will be very bitter. These peoples will become a source of continual stumbling blocks before their eyes and a source of unrest, hardship and exhaustion, and He likened these stumbling blocks to pricks in the eyes and thorns in the sides. And instead of the land being a land of peace, it will become a land of distress, gloom and turmoil. The history of the people has proved this, for throughout the history of Israel some peoples whom they spared were a source of misery and wretchedness to this people.

33.29.0.en: That will not be all, but there will also be a punishment for you from Me, God your Savior, because you made light of My word, so I will take away from you My blessing and My peace, and even punish you with what I am about to punish these peoples with.

33.29.1.en: My friend, do not make light of the Lord's commands and commandments, for they are for your good and your protection first, and the punishment for not carrying them out is also severe.

33.29.2.en: The borders of the new land
